global: Ser {player} marched forth with {troop_count} banners and crawled home with a handful. A sorry tale for the bards.
Let it be recorded that {troop_count} of ser {player}'s finest fell in a single field. I shall not waste my breath on pity.
Who knew the mighty army of ser {player} could be undone so quickly. Perhaps the banners were sewn from wet cloth.
The proud host of ser {player} is scattered across the fields like chaff. I would grieve if I were not so amused.
Ser {player} spoke of conquest at the feast. Now the only conquest is the crows feasting on {troop_count} dead.
A reckoning is owed for every drop of blood lost to ser {player}'s pride. The debt grows, and I will collect it.
Ser {player} led a rout so complete that even the hedgerows fled. Take your remaining men home and count your sins.
Pride goes before the fall, as the old texts say. Ser {player} has now proven the saying true before all watchers.
whisper: Your fine host lies in the mud, ser {player}. I have seen many a proud banner sink, and yours sinks faster.
Do not mistake this defeat for mercy. I know where your remaining men sleep, and I am not so forgiving.
You led {troop_count} good souls to slaughter for a vanity. Their widows will remember, and so will I.
Ser {player}, you bought a lesson with blood. I suggest you learn it quickly, for I shall not teach it twice.
A broken oath and a broken army, ser {player}. Such a pity the one who sealed them both walks free to boast.
Enjoy your retreat, friend. I will be waiting at the crossroads when your banners are patched and proud again.
Ser {player}, the ravens have already chosen your epitaph. I merely wished to spare you the embarrassment of reading it.
I doubt you can afford another march after that rout. Keep your wounded close, ser {player}, and your gates closer.

global: The field near the ford is wet with blood today. Ser {player} has learned what the river takes from the proud.
Word travels that ser {player} lost much on the plain. Let the wise weigh what that means for the coming season.
Ser {player} rode out with {troop_count} and rode back with fewer. I make no judgment, only note the count.
Grievous news from the eastern road. The fallen of ser {player} will be sung of, though not by me tonight.
A battle lost is not a war lost, though the tavern gossip would say otherwise. Patience, all of you.
Hard fortune has visited ser {player}. Let us see whether the banners rise again before the harvest bells ring.
I shall keep my counsel on the defeat of ser {player}. The road ahead is long, and so is memory.
Several banners came home without their riders this morning. Ser {player} will need time, and quiet, to mend.
whisper: I heard of your losses, ser {player}. Should you require provisions for your remaining men, speak plainly and we shall see.
Your defeat is known across the district. I offer no comfort I cannot back with deeds, so do not ask for empty words.
Ser {player}, a fallen army is a heavy thing to carry. I trust you will find your footing before the next muster.
I wish you well in recovering, though I keep my own affairs close. We may yet have business when the dust settles.
Such a heavy blow, ser {player}. I shall not pretend surprise, nor shall I pretend grief. Take care of your remnant.
Rest your men while you may, friend. The roads will not forgive a rider who ignores weary horses and weary hearts.
Do not look to me for vengeance or for charity, ser {player}. Look to your own table, and count what remains.
Whatever befell you on that field, ser {player}, I hope the lessons prove worth the price paid in blood.

global: Ser {player} fought with courage beyond reason, and the field took its bitter price. Honour remains with them.
My heart is heavy for ser {player}, whose host was broken on the plain. May the ancestors guard every fallen soul.
No shame falls on ser {player} for the day's loss. Even the mightiest oaks are sometimes felled by the storm.
Hear me, travellers: ser {player} did not flee from the field, but stood until the last banner fell. Remember it.
The loss of {troop_count} brave souls will be mourned in halls across the land. Ser {player} shall rebuild them.
Let the taverns sing of the valour of ser {player} at the ford, though the songs are sad. Their stand was not in vain.
Friends, a defeat is only a lesson in grief. Gather round ser {player} and offer what aid you can to the living.
Ser {player} carries a heavy burden tonight. I call on all honest folk to lift their cups and steady their hands.
whisper: Ser {player}, I grieve with you. Come to my hall when you are ready, and we will speak of rebuilding.
Do not despair, friend. A host can be raised again from the hearts that remain, and mine is open to you.
You stood where few would stand, ser {player}. That kind of courage is not lost with the fallen banners.
I will send what men and supplies I can spare to your banner. Think no more on debt between us, ser {player}.
The field has taken much from you, ser {player}. Rest tonight, and let the morning bring clearer counsel.
Ser {player}, your sorrow is my sorrow. Should you need a shield in the days ahead, you need only send word.
Remember that a broken host is not a broken name. Yours still rings true among those who witnessed your stand.
Keep your chin high, ser {player}. The ancestors did not build their names on victories alone, but on rising again.
